items.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose a framework to enrich context and selectively enhance robustness of LLM agents in social simulations, addressing behavior brittleness from prompt variations.
items.whyItMatters: It improves reliability of AI-driven social models, crucial for accurate policy and behavioral research.

items.title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
items.summary: FlowReconBench compares ten learned and five classical flow reconstruction methods on sparse sensor data across laminar cylinder wake regimes.
items.whyItMatters: It guides engineers on when machine learning beats traditional models for accurate, calibrated flow predictions.

items.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
items.summary: BEAKER introduces a benchmark for evaluating embodied AI brains in automated chemical labs, focusing on perception, reasoning, and safe action.
items.whyItMatters: It helps gauge AI readiness for autonomous, safe lab experimentation, a key step for rapid scientific discovery.

items.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
items.summary: FrontierPhysics presents a new benchmark of 56 physics tasks, designed by experts to assess AI agents on full research workflows, not just isolated problems.
items.whyItMatters: It pushes AI toward genuine scientific discovery, offering a realistic test of research quality and innovation.

items.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
items.summary: The article discusses how humanoid robots can learn motion from simulation, addressing data scarcity by mapping visual and language inputs to joint commands.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it advances scalable, autonomous robot control without costly real-world data collection.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
items.summary: Reinforcement learning iteratively refines a generalist robot policy trained on a large corpus, improving performance after initial zero‑shot generalization.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers see how RL boosts versatile robot models, making them more practical for real‑world tasks.

items.title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues
items.summary: The paper shows occlusion can be inferred from disagreements between two monocular distance estimates, avoiding the need for explicit occlusion annotations.
items.whyItMatters: It enables robots to detect hidden pedestrians using existing depth cues, improving safety with minimal extra training.

items.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
items.summary: The article analyzes how AI exposure correlates with dull, dirty, and dangerous work conditions across U.S. occupations.
items.whyItMatters: It shows AI could reduce hazardous jobs, informing policy and workforce planning.

items.title: Adaptive Multi Mode: Budget-Aware Routing of Optimizers By Online Landscape Probes
items.summary: Adaptive Multi Mode routes optimizers based on budget and landscape, using online probes to choose among quasi-Newton, trust-region, coordinate, multistart, and evolution strategies.
items.whyItMatters: It improves efficiency for black-box optimization by selecting the best method for each problem’s constraints.

items.title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
items.summary: SpecCompact speeds up LLM agent context compaction by using slot‑parallel semantic speculative verification to balance detail and latency.
items.whyItMatters: It lets agents handle longer histories faster, improving real‑time performance for AI applications.

items.title: Learning to Decode Linear Codes with Generalized Belief Propagation Network
items.summary: The paper introduces GBPNet, a neural decoder that improves linear code decoding by preserving message‑passing symmetry.
items.whyItMatters: It offers better error‑correcting performance for reliable, high‑speed communications.

items.title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
items.summary: The paper tests turn-level best‑of‑N sampling, where a generator produces N actions and a selector picks one, to improve LLM agents on long‑horizon tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a lightweight, inference‑time method to boost agent performance without costly training.

items.title: CounterFactual Retrieval for Evidence-Aware Individual Animal Identification
items.summary: Automated identification of individual animals is moving from small curated studies toward shared benchmarks and reusable foundation models. This progress is useful, but current evaluation leaves the evidence behind a match unresolved, i.e., high retrieval accuracy does not show whether a model used animal features or identity-correlated shortcuts. items.title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
items.summary: Hierarchical text embedding models offer variable-length representations, while quantization reduces numerical precision; both aim to improve computational efficiency. This work is an empirical benchmark study of how these two orthogonal, already-established techniques interact. We evaluate 38 tasks from the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) using four transformer-based embedding models…

items.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source…

items.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
items.summary: We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation. The task requires retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, binding entities and relations, and composing one coherent final image from multiple references. items.title: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) have recently achieved superhuman performance on several long-horizon benchmarks. However, their computational cost limits their use in long-horizon tasks and real-time domains such as video games. A key bottleneck is representing each screenshot as thousands of visual tokens, which accumulate into long contexts as agents reason over extended interaction histories. We…

items.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
items.summary: Common methods for monitoring features in large language models (LLMs) such as linear probes and sparse autoencoders (SAEs) assume that features maintain a consistent representation across contexts. LLMs, however, can flexibly adopt different perspectives or "personas" that suggest different underlying systems of conceptual relations. items.title: Navigating Disagreement Among Criteria for Evaluating Explanation Faithfulness
items.summary: Faithfulness requires that algorithmic explanations accurately reflect the model's behavior. Yet existing operationalizations of faithfulness can disagree about whether the same explanation is faithful, leaving developers and auditors to choose among conflicting evaluations. In this paper, we investigate disagreement among evaluation criteria and offer a practical path forward for evaluating…

items.title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
items.summary: Grain growth during heat treatment strongly affects the microstructure of polycrystalline materials and, consequently, their mechanical properties. Although numerical methods such as front-tracking or front-capturing simulations can accurately describe grain growth, their high computational cost limits their use for long or non-isothermal thermal cycles.
